meta.name: insights_interpretable_db
notes: This is a human-interpretable trait library + unmoderated questionnaire + scoring rules inspired by the public-facing concepts of Insights Discovery colour energies.
It is NOT the proprietary Insights Discovery Preference Evaluator, and does not replicate proprietary scoring keys or item wording.
v1.1 adds gamification design spec, a report template modelled on an Insights-style team report, and generation rules for higher-quality narrative outputs.

cool_blue.core_drive: accuracy, understanding, quality, control of risk
typical_behaviours: Defines criteria, checks assumptions, asks for evidence
Structures work into processes, standards, documentation
Notices inconsistencies, spots defects, improves systems
communication_cues: Precise language, measured tone, preference for written detail
Asks: What’s the data, what’s the definition, what’s the risk
strengths: Rigour, objectivity, critical thinking, quality assurance
blind_spots: Over-analyses, delays decisions, appears critical or distant
Undervalues emotion, morale, and informal networks
best_environment: Clear standards, time to think, access to data, logical debate
how_to_work_with: Bring evidence, define the decision, agree criteria, give time to reflect

earth_green.core_drive: harmony, trust, values, care, sustainable pace
typical_behaviours: Builds rapport, checks impact on people, seeks inclusion
Listens, supports, develops others, mediates conflict
Prefers steady progress and shared ownership
communication_cues: Asks: How will this land, who is affected
strengths: Coaching, collaboration, relationship repair, team culture
blind_spots: Avoids conflict, softens messages, tolerates poor performance too long
Prioritises consensus over speed and clarity
under_pressure: More accommodating, reassurance-seeking, or withdraws to protect relationships
best_environment: Psychological safety, time for consultation, clear values, respectful dialogue
how_to_work_with: Show empathy, explain people impact, invite input, avoid public confrontation

typical_behaviours: Generates ideas, spots opportunities, enjoys experimentation
Networks, motivates, tells stories, builds momentum through energy
communication_cues: Asks: What’s possible, what’s the big picture
strengths: Creativity, persuasion, change energy, engagement, brainstorming
blind_spots: Lacks follow-through, skips details, over-promises, gets distracted
Talks more than listens when excited
under_pressure: More talkative, restless, scattered, seeks stimulation via interaction
best_environment: Autonomy, variety, social contact, room for experimentation
how_to_work_with: Start with the vision, keep it interactive, agree next steps and owners in writing

typical_behaviours: Makes fast decisions, pushes through obstacles, takes charge
Comfortable with disagreement, sets ambitious targets
communication_cues: Asks: What’s the goal, what are we doing now
strengths: Decisiveness, execution, negotiating, driving change, crisis response
blind_spots: Blunt, impatient, dismissive when under time pressure
Under-invests in consultation, nuance, or relationship repair
under_pressure: More forceful, impatient, controlling, escalates conflict to move forward
best_environment: Clear goals, autonomy, fast feedback loops, measurable outcomes
how_to_work_with: Be brief and prepared, propose options, agree decisions and deadlines, avoid waffle

combination_blurbs.label: Red–Blue
combination_blurbs.blurb: Decisive and rigorous. Drives outcomes with logic, can be blunt and demanding.

combination_blurbs.label: Red–Yellow
combination_blurbs.blurb: Fast and influential. Energises action, can skip detail and over-commit.

combination_blurbs.label: Red–Green
combination_blurbs.blurb: Protective leader. Pushes for results while caring for people, can feel torn between speed and harmony.

combination_blurbs.label: Blue–Green
combination_blurbs.blurb: Thoughtful and considerate. High standards plus empathy, can deliberate and avoid hard calls.

combination_blurbs.label: Blue–Yellow
combination_blurbs.blurb: Curious analyst. Ideas plus logic, can oscillate between exploration and critique.

combination_blurbs.label: Green–Yellow
combination_blurbs.blurb: Supportive connector. Builds community and enthusiasm, can avoid confrontation and drift from priorities.

primary_secondary.definition: Highest score is dominant energy; second highest is secondary energy. Use to generate narrative: default gear plus accessible alternative gear.

guidance.flat_profile: Scores cluster tightly. Interpret cautiously. Validate with behaviour checks.
guidance.moderate: Some clear preferences. Interpret with normal confidence.
guidance.high: Strong preferences. Easier to predict. Watch for interpersonal friction in low-energy areas.

red_vs_green.definition: Task and pace versus people and harmony

blue_vs_yellow.definition: Precision and analysis versus spontaneity and enthusiasm

questionnaire.title: Workplace behaviour preferences questionnaire (colour energies)
instructions: Answer based on how you typically behave at work, not how you want to be.
Use the last 4 weeks as your reference period.
Do not overthink. If unsure, pick your default.

items.text: I prefer decisions backed by data and clear criteria.
I enjoy turning messy problems into structured plans.
I notice errors and inconsistencies quickly.
I feel satisfied when standards and procedures are followed.
I check in on how people are coping before pushing the work forward.
I adjust my approach to preserve relationships.
I listen for what is not being said and respond with care.
I prefer decisions that protect team cohesion even if they take longer.
I energise groups by sharing possibilities and ideas.
I like variety and get bored with repetition.
I persuade through enthusiasm and a compelling narrative.
I think out loud and use conversation to generate options.
I get to the point quickly and expect others to do the same.
I am comfortable challenging others directly when needed.
I prioritise speed of execution over perfect information.
I take charge naturally when the goal is clear.
Under pressure, I become more focused on logic, details, and control.
Under pressure, I become more focused on people’s needs and reassurance.
Under pressure, I become more upbeat, talkative, and idea driven.
Under pressure, I become more forceful, decisive, and impatient with delays.
I prefer written communication that is precise and complete.
I prefer communication that is warm, personal, and considerate.
I prefer communication that is lively, expressive, and informal.
I prefer communication that is brief, direct, and action oriented.
A: I would rather be respected for competence than liked for friendliness.  B: I would rather be liked for friendliness than respected for competence.
A: I push for a decision even if not everyone agrees.  B: I hold the decision to build agreement.
A: I enjoy debating to test ideas.  B: I avoid debate if it risks tension.
A: I prefer a clear plan before starting.  B: I prefer to start and adapt as I go.
A: I focus on outcomes and results first.  B: I focus on people and impact first.
A: I keep meetings tight and task focused.  B: I keep meetings open to explore and connect.
A: I value accuracy and quality over speed.  B: I value speed and momentum over accuracy.
A: I want facts and options.  B: I want reassurance and alignment.

confidence.definition: Confidence in the mapping based on signal strength (spread and top gap) plus forced-choice alignment. Not verification against proprietary systems.

narrative_rules: Use dominant_colour core_drive and strengths as the opening.
Add secondary_colour as the accessible alternative gear.
Add one combination_blurb matching the top two colours (order-insensitive).
Add 2 blind_spots: one from dominant_colour and one from lowest-scoring colour.
Generate 3 next_steps: one behaviour to amplify, one to mitigate, one experiment for 2 weeks.

cool_blue: Pre-commit decision criteria and a time-box to avoid analysis paralysis.
Translate your conclusions into a simple one-page action plan for others.
Ask explicitly for the people-impact risks so you do not miss them.
earth_green: Practise giving one clear, direct message per week without cushioning.
Time-box consensus: consult, decide, communicate, then revisit after delivery.
Use written decision logs to reduce ambiguity and prevent drift.
sunshine_yellow: Convert ideas into numbered options with owners and dates within 24 hours.
Schedule a weekly ‘close-out’ slot to finish what you start.
Ask for a ‘what could go wrong’ review before committing publicly.
fiery_red: Add a short consultation step: who is affected and what is the risk.
Replace urgency with clarity: define outcome, constraints, and next milestone.
Practise one ‘slow down to speed up’ decision per week: criteria then commit.

minimum_features: Scoring engine producing 0–6 colour spectrum + derived metrics + confidence score
Human-readable report: traits, strengths, blind spots, under pressure, advice, next steps
Gamified progression: XP, levels, badges, quests, challenges (opt-in)
Two modes: Individual report and Team report (team mode optional)
Reflection prompts and behaviour experiment tracker (14-day)
Achievements screen and challenge library by colour

principles.name: Visible progress
principles.why: Users stay engaged when they can see progress and proximity to milestones.

principles.name: Commitment loops
principles.why: Short, repeatable loops create habit and reduce drop-off.
implementation_notes: Offer a 7-day goal and a streak counter for completing micro-actions (e.g., 'review your top energy' daily).
Allow limited 'streak protection' tokens to reduce catastrophic failure (optional).
source_examples: Duolingo streaks (industry pattern, treat as speculative unless you adopt official sources)

principles.name: Challenges and trophies
principles.why: Time-boxed challenges and achievements convert intentions into action.
implementation_notes: Create challenges aligned to each colour (e.g., Blue: 'Decision criteria in 10 minutes', Red: 'Consult 2 stakeholders before deciding').
Award trophies when a challenge is completed; keep a persistent 'Achievements' view.
source_examples: Nike Run Club challenges and trophies

principles.name: Tiered progression and rewards
principles.why: Tiers provide status and unlocks as engagement grows.
implementation_notes: Introduce tiers for learning completion and practice: Explorer -> Builder -> Leader.
Unlock deeper sections of the report and optional team modules as users complete follow-up actions.

principles.name: Choice and personalisation
principles.why: Users engage more when they choose paths that fit their goals.
implementation_notes: After results, let users pick one of three tracks (communication, decision-making, collaboration).
Tailor quests to dominant and lowest colours.

principles.name: Social mechanics with guardrails
principles.why: Social comparison boosts engagement but can harm users if mishandled.
implementation_notes: Default to private progress. Offer opt-in team challenges and anonymised cohorts.
Avoid global leaderboards unless you can protect privacy and reduce unhealthy competition.

xp.description: Points for completing questionnaire, reading report, completing next steps.

badges.name: Team Ready
badges.criteria: Invite 2+ colleagues to a team session (optional).

cool_blue.title: Criteria in 10
cool_blue.description: Before a decision, write 3 decision criteria and 1 key risk in under 10 minutes.

cool_blue.title: One-page clarity
cool_blue.description: Convert a complex plan into a one-page summary with owners and dates.

earth_green.title: Kind but clear
earth_green.description: Deliver one direct message with empathy, without cushioning or delaying.

earth_green.title: Two-minute check-in
earth_green.description: Do a 2-minute check-in with one colleague before pushing a deadline.

sunshine_yellow.title: Ideas to options
sunshine_yellow.description: Turn 3 ideas into 3 numbered options with pros/cons and a decision date.

sunshine_yellow.title: Close-out Friday
sunshine_yellow.description: Finish one open loop before starting something new.

fiery_red.title: Consult 2
fiery_red.description: Before a big decision, ask 2 stakeholders for risks and constraints, then decide.

fiery_red.title: Outcome and constraints
fiery_red.description: Write the outcome, constraints, and next milestone in 3 bullet points.

tiers.name: Leader
tiers.criteria: Complete 1 two-week experiment and generate a team report (optional).

individual_report_v1.purpose: Provide a clear, actionable analysis of an individual’s colour energy spectrum, with strengths, challenges, communication tips, and a practical development plan.
sections: Purpose and how to use this report
generation_rules: Profile summary: 120–180 words, anchored to dominant+secondary energies, avoid clinical language.
Strengths: pick 5 bullets: 3 from dominant, 2 from secondary; deduplicate by meaning.
Challenges: pick 5 bullets: 3 from lowest energy blind-spots, 2 from dominant blind-spots.
Communication tips: 4 bullets derived from how_to_work_with dominant/secondary, plus 1 watch-out related to lowest energy.
Next steps: pick 3 from next_steps_library (dominant, lowest, and one from secondary). Create a 14-day experiment using one relevant challenge.

team_report_v1.purpose: Provide a comprehensive analysis of a team based on individual colour energy profiles to optimise communication, collaboration, and performance.
team_report_v1.modelled_on: Insights Discovery Team Report example structure
sections: Conscious vs less conscious summary (if available)
Specialist areas: Client interaction (internal and external)
generation_rules: Each individual gets: role label (optional), dominant and less dominant colours, 120–180 word profile summary, plus Strengths/Challenges/Communication Tips lists.
Team analysis: summarise diversity, balance, interpersonal dynamics, conflict style, motivation patterns; keep it behaviour-specific.
Specialist areas: output playbooks as numbered actions; include meeting agenda patterns and role allocation.
Pairings: for each pair, list synergy, friction risk, and 2 operating agreements.

must_have: Explainability: show numbers and how they map to text
Actionability: next steps are specific, time-boxed, measurable
Balanced: strengths and risks, not only positives
Privacy: avoid sharing results with others without consent

post_results: Which two behaviours in the report feel most accurate, and why (one example each)?
Which one risk or blind spot feels most relevant right now, and what triggers it?
What is one small change you can run for 14 days to improve outcomes?
weekly_checkin: What went well this week that aligns with your dominant energy?
Where did your lowest energy show up as a friction point?
What is the one adjustment you will make next week?
